Reproduction: damid.py run executed in a scratch copy of the tree (original result.json untouched, sha256 efa3b8a6... unchanged); stdout is identical to logs/damid.log and the regenerated result.json is byte-identical to damid/results/result.json.

Caveat (design, already disclosed): P_batch and P_all are not independent replications; both rest on the same LMNA KO clone 14 vs WT clone 17 and share LMNAKO_r2. Clonal drift cannot be excluded; the claim is one clone pair in one cell line.

Caveat (null): the within-chromosome shift null is not centred at zero for the placebos (null means -0.038 PL_within, +0.042 PL_cross) because chromosome-level GC/delta structure survives the shift. Primaries' null means are ~0 (-0.010, +0.009), so primary p-values and the label are unaffected, but placebo p-values should not be read against zero.

Caveat (interpretation): LBR KO and DKO vs WT give the opposite sign (+0.27 to +0.33) together with compressed dynamic range (SD 1.69-1.73 vs 2.45-2.51) and baseline slopes of -0.40/-0.44, showing that GC~delta is very sensitive to range differences. LMNA KO SD is ~3-8% above WT, the direction that would push GC rho negative; the scale-free arm (rho unchanged) and near-zero baseline slopes argue against this driving the result, but z-scoring removes only a global linear scale difference, not GC-dependent (e.g. LAD-strength-nonlinear) range changes.

Supporting (exploratory): DKO_r2 - LBRKO_r3 (same batch r8, i.e. LMNA loss on an LBR-null background) gives rho -0.145 (p 0.001), same sign as the registered primaries, although the lineage of the LBR KO clone relative to clone 14 is not established.

No flaw found that should change the label. The report's REPLICATED statement and disclosed limits are accurate; recommend adding the shared-clone non-independence of the two primaries and the placebo null offset to the report.
